@pubsubOperation.summary: Subscribes a GraphQL field (usually on `Subscription`) to a named event topic so clients receive events as GraphQL subscription payloads (EDFS-style event-driven subscriptions).

authors.intro:
Import with `@link(url: "https://specs.graphql-mesh.dev/pubsub/v0.1", import: ["@pubsubOperation"])` (and `@composeDirective` when the Supergraph must carry the directive). Put `@pubsubOperation` on the field that should stream events. Pair each topic with one or more `@pubsubPublish` (or other publishers) that emit the same topic string.

EDFS model (authors): Events travel on a shared topic bus. A publisher puts a payload on a topic; every active `@pubsubOperation` subscription on that topic receives it as the next GraphQL subscription event. Topics are ordinary strings you choose (`"new_product"`, `"todoAdded"`, …). The special form `webhook:<method>:<path>` (method lowercase, path as served) means “also accept that HTTP request as an event on this topic” when webhook HTTP ingress is enabled — the request body becomes the payload.

implementers.intro:
Implement **event-driven federated subscriptions (EDFS)** from this page alone: a topic bus plus two directive behaviors. You do not need Mesh source to follow the contract.

Topic bus: Provide publish(topic, payload) and subscribe(topic) → async iterator of payloads. Topics are opaque strings compared for equality (after any documented interpolation). The same string ties publishers to subscribers.

`webhook:<method>:<path>` topics: When webhook ingress is enabled, an HTTP request whose method (lowercase) and path match the topic must publish the request body (JSON if `Content-Type` is JSON, otherwise raw text) on that topic and acknowledge (e.g. 204). If ingress is disabled, treat webhook topics like any other string or reject them consistently.

`@pubsubOperation` field: For each annotated field (typically under `Subscription`), install a `subscribe` that listens on `pubsubTopic` and a `resolve` that returns the event payload as the field value (or a documented projection). Multiple apps on one field all listen; merge iterators or subscribe once per distinct topic as you prefer. Interpolation of `{args.*}` / `{context.*}` in the topic string is allowed if you document it; otherwise treat the topic as literal.

Composition: Preserve the directive on the Supergraph (`@composeDirective` / equivalent). `subgraph`, when present, must be the same composition subgraph name used elsewhere for that source.
implementers.compose: Schemas emit `@link` to this family URL and apply `@pubsubOperation` on subscription fields. Keep the directive through Supergraph composition so the runtime can wire listeners.
implementers.runtime: On schema load, for every `@pubsubOperation` field: bind subscribe → bus.subscribe(topic); resolve → payload (identity unless you define projection). For webhook topics, register HTTP routes when ingress is on. Client GraphQL subscriptions then receive bus events as field payloads.
implementers.validation: Require a non-empty `pubsubTopic` for executable subscriptions. Webhook topics must match `webhook:<method>:<path>` with a lowercase method. `subgraph`, when present, must match the composition subgraph name.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute the directive to that composition subgraph name. Use the same string as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and other directives for the source. Never invent a second name for the same source.

pubsubTopic.defaults: Required for a working subscription (SDL may leave it optional; empty topics are useless).
pubsubTopic.constraints: Non-empty topic string. Ordinary topics are free-form. Webhook form: `webhook:<method>:<path>` with lowercase method (e.g. `post`) and the path the HTTP ingress will see.
pubsubTopic.authors: Topic to listen on. Must match the topic publishers use. Prefer the webhook form when external HTTP callbacks should drive the subscription.
pubsubTopic.implementers: Pass to the bus subscribe API. For webhook topics, also bind HTTP method+path → publish on that topic when ingress is enabled.
pubsubTopic.validation: Reject empty topics. Webhook form: `webhook:` + lowercase method + `:` + path.

@pubsubPublish.summary: After a field resolves successfully, publishes that field’s result to a named topic so `@pubsubOperation` (and other) subscribers receive it (EDFS publisher side).

authors.intro:
Import with `@link(url: "https://specs.graphql-mesh.dev/pubsub/v0.1", import: ["@pubsubPublish"])`. Annotate Mutation (or Query) fields whose successful result should notify subscribers. Use the **same** `pubsubTopic` string as the matching `@pubsubOperation`.

EDFS model (authors): Resolve the field as usual (create/update/…). Then the runtime publishes the returned value on the topic. Subscribers on that topic get the next event. Publishing is part of delivering the GraphQL response for that field: if publish fails, the client can see a field error even though the mutation’s side effect already happened — there is no automatic rollback.

implementers.intro:
Publisher half of EDFS. After the original field resolver returns a value, publish that value on `pubsubTopic` for every `@pubsubPublish` app on the field, then return the same value to the GraphQL response.

Ordering / errors: Await all publish jobs before completing the field. If any publish rejects, surface a GraphQL field error; do not undo the resolver’s side effect. If the bus is missing, treat as implementer-defined (error vs no-op); A conforming runtime must provide a topic bus when these directives are used.

Payload: Publish the field result as-is unless you document a projection. Subscribers’ `resolve` typically returns that payload as the subscription field value.

Composition: Preserve the directive on the Supergraph. Match `subgraph` names to composition identifiers when present.
implementers.compose: Keep `@pubsubPublish` on the Supergraph so the gateway can wrap annotated fields. No special join rewrite beyond preserving args.
implementers.runtime: Wrap the field resolver: result = await original(); for each app, await publish(app.pubsubTopic, result); return result. Propagate publish failures as field errors.
implementers.validation: Require a non-empty `pubsubTopic` for executable publishers. `subgraph`, when present, must match the composition subgraph name.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute the directive to that composition subgraph name. Use the same string as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and other directives for the source. Never invent a second name for the same source.

pubsubTopic.defaults: Required to publish (empty topics do nothing useful).
pubsubTopic.constraints: Topic string shared with `@pubsubOperation` subscribers (and any external bus consumers).
pubsubTopic.authors: Destination topic for the field’s resolved value. Must match subscriber topics exactly.
pubsubTopic.implementers: Publish the field result to this topic after a successful resolve; await completion before returning.
pubsubTopic.validation: Reject empty topics; must equal the subscriber topic string exactly when pairing with `@pubsubOperation`.
